Python API Reference¶

These pages document the authored Python API that provider authors use to build Gestalt integrations, authentication providers, caches, and S3 backends.

Public authoring surface for Gestalt Python providers.

The package is published as gestalt-sdk and imported as gestalt. Use it for executable provider code: integration operations, host-service providers, host-service clients, and provider-owned telemetry.

from gestalt import Model, App, operation

class SearchInput(Model):
    query: str

app = App("search")

@app.operation(title="Search")
def search(params: SearchInput):
    return {"query": params.query}

Transport internals are owned by the SDK. Provider code should use the authored helpers exported here.

The supported import surface is the top-level gestalt package:

from gestalt import Model, App, Cache, IndexedDB, S3

This reference focuses on provider-facing classes, helpers, clients, and native input models. Transport serialization details are intentionally omitted.

Core authoring types¶

Model

Base class for operation input and output models.

field

Declare a model field with catalog metadata.

Subject

Identity information attached to an incoming provider request.

Credential

Credential metadata resolved by the Gestalt host for the request.

Access

Authorization context resolved for the request.

Request

Host-provided request context for an operation invocation.

Response

Structured operation response with an explicit HTTP status.

OK

Wrap body in a success response with status 200 OK.

Error

Application error raised by a provider operation.
class Model¶

Base class for operation input and output models.

Subclasses are automatically converted into dataclasses, so provider authors can declare request and response types with normal annotations:

class SearchInput(Model):
    query: str = field(description="Search term")
field(*, description='', default=MISSING, default_factory=MISSING, required=None)¶

Declare a model field with catalog metadata.

Parameters:

  • description (str) – Human-readable parameter description exported to the generated catalog.

  • default (Any) – Explicit default value for the field.

  • default_factory (Any) – Callable used to create the default value.

  • required (bool | None) – Override the inferred required flag in the generated catalog.

Return type:

Any

App authoring¶

App

Integration app definition and operation registry.

operation

Register an operation on the calling module's implicit app.

session_catalog

Register a per-request catalog hook on the implicit module app.

http_subject

Register a hosted HTTP subject hook on the implicit module app.

HTTPSubjectRequest

Host-provided HTTP request data for resolving a hosted subject.

HTTPSubjectResolutionError

Raised by subject handlers to reject a hosted HTTP request.

http_subject_error

Return an error that rejects hosted HTTP subject resolution.

SessionCatalogProvider

Protocol for apps that return a per-request catalog.

Catalog

CatalogOperation

CatalogParameter

OperationAnnotations

class App(name, *, module_name=None)¶

Integration app definition and operation registry.

App collects operation handlers, optional configuration hooks, and optional session catalog hooks before handing control to the runtime:

from gestalt import Model, App

class SearchInput(Model):
    query: str

app = App("search")

@app.operation(title="Search")
def search(params: SearchInput):
    return {"query": params.query}
Parameters:

  • name (str)

  • module_name (str | None)

operation(func=None, /, *, id=None, method=DEFAULT_OPERATION_METHOD, title='', description='', allowed_roles=None, tags=None, read_only=False, visible=None)¶

Register an operation on the calling module’s implicit app.

This decorator is useful when a module-level app object would be redundant:

from gestalt import Model, operation

class SearchInput(Model):
    query: str

@operation(title="Search")
def search(params: SearchInput):
    return {"query": params.query}

Workflow helpers¶

These helpers build workflow values from native Python inputs. Structured payload fields accept JSON-compatible mappings or dataclass instances. Timestamp fields accept datetime values, and copy helpers return non-aliased message copies.

BoundWorkflowTarget

Native data for a bound workflow target.

WorkflowStep

Native data for one workflow step.

WorkflowStepAppCall

Native data for a workflow app step call.

WorkflowStepAgentTurn

Native data for a workflow agent step turn.

WorkflowValue

Native data for a workflow value expression.

WorkflowActivation

Native data for a compiled workflow activation.

WorkflowDefinitionSpec

Native data for applying a workflow definition.

WorkflowDefinition

Native data copied from a workflow-provider definition.

WorkflowRun

Native data for a workflow-provider run.

WorkflowStepExecution

Native data for one durable workflow step execution.

WorkflowRunEvent

Run event returned by workflow providers.

bound_workflow_target

Create a bound workflow target.

bound_workflow_target_from_target

Return a deep copy of a bound workflow target.

workflow_step

Create a workflow step.

workflow_step_app_call

Create a workflow app step call.

workflow_step_agent_turn

Create a workflow agent step turn.

workflow_value

Create a workflow value expression.

workflow_definition_spec

Create a workflow definition spec.

workflow_definition

Create a workflow-provider definition.

workflow_event

Create a workflow event .

workflow_event_from_event

Return a deep copy of a workflow event.

workflow_signal

Create a workflow signal .

workflow_signal_from_signal

Return a deep copy of a workflow signal.

workflow_run_trigger

Create a workflow run trigger .

workflow_run_trigger_from_trigger

Return a deep copy of a workflow run trigger.

workflow_run

Create a workflow-provider run.

workflow_run_from_run

Return a deep copy of a workflow-provider run.

Agent provider models¶

Agent providers receive and return native dataclasses. Structured payload fields accept JSON-compatible mappings or dataclass instances, and timestamp fields on sessions, turns, events, interactions, and host connections use timezone-aware datetime values. The runtime owns transport serialization.

Provider interfaces¶

Base interface shared by provider-style runtimes.

Optional mixin for providers that expose descriptive metadata.

HealthChecker

Optional mixin for providers that support health checks.

Starter

Optional mixin for providers with an explicit post-configure start phase.

WarningsProvider

Optional mixin for providers that emit startup warnings.

Closer

Optional mixin for providers with explicit shutdown work.

AppProviderAdapter

Wrap a provider and registration callback for integration runtimes.

AuthenticationProvider

Base class for authentication providers.

ExternalTokenValidator

Optional mixin for providers that validate external bearer tokens.

SessionTTLProvider

Optional mixin for providers that control session lifetimes.

SecretsProvider

Base class for secret-provider runtimes.

CacheProvider

Base class for cache-provider runtimes.

S3Provider

Base class for S3-compatible object store runtimes.

AgentProvider

RuntimeProvider

Base class for hosted runtime providers.

WorkflowProvider

AuthenticatedUser

Authenticated user returned by an authentication provider.

Provider telemetry¶

gestaltd configures OpenTelemetry exporters from the selected providers.telemetry entry and passes standard OTEL_* environment into provider processes. Python providers that run through the SDK runtime get that setup automatically and can use gestalt.telemetry for provider-authored GenAI spans and metrics.

OpenTelemetry helpers for provider-authored GenAI instrumentation.

The Gestalt runtime configures exporters from host-provided OTEL_* environment before a provider starts serving. Provider code should use this module to create GenAI semantic-convention spans and metrics around the model, agent, and tool work it owns.

Operation

Context manager that records a GenAI span plus duration and token metrics.

configure_from_environment

Configure OpenTelemetry exporters from standard OTEL environment variables.

shutdown

Flush and shut down configured OpenTelemetry providers.

model_operation

Create a GenAI chat/model operation around an upstream model SDK call.

agent_invocation

Create a GenAI agent invocation operation for a provider-owned turn.

tool_execution

Create a GenAI tool execution operation.

record_openai_usage

Record token usage fields from an OpenAI SDK response.

record_anthropic_usage

Record token usage fields from an Anthropic SDK response.
GENAI_PROVIDER_NAME = 'gestalt'¶

str(object=’’) -> str str(bytes_or_buffer[, encoding[, errors]]) -> str

Create a new string object from the given object. If encoding or errors is specified, then the object must expose a data buffer that will be decoded using the given encoding and error handler. Otherwise, returns the result of object.__str__() (if defined) or repr(object). encoding defaults to ‘utf-8’. errors defaults to ‘strict’.

GENAI_OPERATION_CHAT = 'chat'¶

CURSOR_NEXT = 0¶

int([x]) -> integer int(x, base=10) -> integer

Convert a number or string to an integer, or return 0 if no arguments are given. If x is a number, return x.__int__(). For floating-point numbers, this truncates towards zero.

If x is not a number or if base is given, then x must be a string, bytes, or bytearray instance representing an integer literal in the given base. The literal can be preceded by ‘+’ or ‘-’ and be surrounded by whitespace. The base defaults to 10. Valid bases are 0 and 2-36. Base 0 means to interpret the base from the string as an integer literal. >>> int(‘0b100’, base=0) 4

CURSOR_NEXT_UNIQUE = 1¶

int([x]) -> integer int(x, base=10) -> integer

Convert a number or string to an integer, or return 0 if no arguments are given. If x is a number, return x.__int__(). For floating-point numbers, this truncates towards zero.

If x is not a number or if base is given, then x must be a string, bytes, or bytearray instance representing an integer literal in the given base. The literal can be preceded by ‘+’ or ‘-’ and be surrounded by whitespace. The base defaults to 10. Valid bases are 0 and 2-36. Base 0 means to interpret the base from the string as an integer literal. >>> int(‘0b100’, base=0) 4

The literal can be preceded by ‘+’ or ‘-’ and be surrounded by whitespace. The base defaults to 10. Valid bases are 0 and 2-36. Base 0 means to interpret the base from the string as an integer literal. >>> int(‘0b100’, base=0) 4

Host service clients¶

These clients connect to host services made available to a provider process by gestaltd.

ENV_RUNTIME_SESSION_ID

str(object='') -> str str(bytes_or_buffer[, encoding[, errors]]) -> str

Agent

Client for managing agent sessions, turns, events, and interactions.

AppProtocol

Fakeable contract for app invocation calls.

RuntimeLogHost

Client for appending runtime logs to the host log stream.

RuntimeLogWriter

File-like object that forwards writes to RuntimeLogHost.

RuntimeLogHandler

Python logging handler that forwards records to runtime logs.

Workflow

Client for applying definitions, starting runs, signaling, and delivering events.
ENV_RUNTIME_SESSION_ID = 'GESTALT_RUNTIME_SESSION_ID'¶

str(object=’’) -> str str(bytes_or_buffer[, encoding[, errors]]) -> str

Create a new string object from the given object. If encoding or errors is specified, then the object must expose a data buffer that will be decoded using the given encoding and error handler. Otherwise, returns the result of object.__str__() (if defined) or repr(object). encoding defaults to ‘utf-8’. errors defaults to ‘strict’.

class RuntimeLogHost¶

Client for appending runtime logs to the host log stream.

RuntimeLogHost reads GESTALT_HOST_SERVICE_SOCKET and its optional relay token from the environment. Use it directly for structured log entries, or create a RuntimeLogWriter/RuntimeLogHandler when redirecting standard streams or Python logging output.

Generated provider clients¶

Each provider service ships a typed module under gestalt that pairs native dataclasses for request and response payloads with one gRPC client class per service. Docstrings come from the service definitions, and gestalt.rpc_support carries the shared error model and the native JsonValue representation used by structured payload fields.

Shared support: gestalt.rpc_support¶

Public support surface for generated Gestalt SDK clients: the canonical error model and the native representations of well-known types that appear in generated signatures. The call helpers and wire converters live in the internal _codec package.

JsonValue = bool | int | float | str | list['JsonValue'] | dict[str, 'JsonValue'] | None¶

The native representation of a JSON value carried in structured payloads.

idempotency_key: str¶

The provider mints the session id returned on AgentSession. Creation is idempotent on idempotency_key scoped per subject (created_by_subject_id): a replayed key returns the existing session, an empty key always creates. Idempotency is scoped to the provider’s session store.

class Agent(channel)¶

Agent is the authoritative agent data boundary. Read RPCs for sessions, turns, turn events, and interactions should use provider-owned control-plane state and should not require a live execution sandbox, pod-level transport, or cached tunnel.

Client for the gestalt.provider.v1.Agent service.
